summary:
Palau decriminalised consensual same-sex conduct in 2014. The Penal Code signed by the President in April 2014 dropped the sodomy offence formerly at section 2803 of Chapter 28, "Sex Crimes", Title 17, which carried up to ten years' imprisonment. Palau's Attorney General confirmed the repeal to Human Dignity Trust, and no offence against consensual same-sex conduct is in force.

Before that repeal, Palau appeared on a list of more than 70 Pacific and global jurisdictions whose laws still criminalised same-sex relations, published around 2011 by the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights. Palau and Nauru both accepted recommendations to decriminalise homosexual acts during their Human Rights Council Universal Periodic Review appearances, which documents a stated commitment to repeal rather than an unannounced change.

At its 2011 Universal Periodic Review, Palau also accepted recommendations to combat discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity. On 22 March 2011 Palau was among the 84 countries on whose behalf Colombia delivered a joint statement to the Human Rights Council calling for an end to violence and human-rights violations based on sexual orientation and gender identity. That statement is the earliest dated record of the government's position in the sources.
tangentialFactors:
The 2014 repeal, taken together with São Tomé and Príncipe's, reduced the global count of countries criminalising anti-sodomy provisions to 79 at the time of reporting. Palau is therefore one of a small number of jurisdictions that legislated repeal rather than inheriting decriminalisation from a colonial-era reform.

Palau's record sits alongside Nauru's in the same Pacific review cycle, where both states accepted decriminalisation recommendations. The regional pattern in the sources is one of repeal and stated commitment rather than active prosecution, but the inventory contains no enforcement data, no reported prosecutions before or after 2014, and no evidence about how the repeal is applied in practice.

The 2011 joint statement Palau joined was delivered on its behalf by Colombia, so the position recorded is Palau's endorsement of a multilateral text rather than a domestic legislative act.
localsOnly:
The 2014 Penal Code applies to conduct within Palau's jurisdiction without distinction between residents and visitors, so the sodomy offence at section 2803 no longer binds Palau residents either. The repeal is a statutory change confirmed at the level of the Attorney General, not a court ruling.

The Universal Periodic Review recommendations Palau accepted in 2011 are commitments addressed to Palau's own government about domestic law and policy, covering both decriminalisation and combating discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity. Residents are the beneficiaries of any discrimination measures flowing from those recommendations; the sources do not identify a specific anti-discrimination statute enacted in response.

Palau's endorsement of the March 2011 joint statement commits it internationally to opposing violence and human-rights violations based on sexual orientation and gender identity, a standard against which its domestic conduct can be assessed.
outOfScopeNotes:
Legal gender recognition is unresolved in the sources: the inventory contains no provision, procedure or refusal governing change of name or gender marker for Palau residents or visitors, and no statement that such a path exists or does not exist.

Hate-crime provisions, statutory anti-discrimination protection covering gender identity, bathroom and facilities rules, healthcare access rules, and recognition of partners or marriages are not sourced here. Their status in Palau is not established by this inventory and should not be read as either present or absent.

Entry, visa and border-screening rules for transgender travellers are not covered by any source in this inventory.

The decriminalisation claim rests on a 2014 report by 76crimes citing Human Dignity Trust and the Attorney General's confirmation. The underlying Penal Code text and the current consolidated statute have not been checked directly, and no source post-dates 2014 to confirm that section 2803 has not been reinstated.
